title: What Happens If They Don't Finish Storyworth in a Year?
summary: Nothing expires if the Storyworth year ends unfinished. Stories stay editable, photos can still be added, and the book prints whenever the storyteller is ready.
body_markdown:
It is the most sensible question anyone asks before buying Storyworth, and it usually comes out slightly apologetically. You want to give something meaningful. You don't want to give something that sits unfinished and turns into one more thing your mother feels guilty about.


So here is the plain answer. Nothing bad happens, nothing expires, and the book still gets made.


## A year of questions is a rhythm


A question arrives once a week for a year by email or text. This cadence is there to give the project a shape, because open-ended projects are the ones that never start or never finish. It is not a quota. Missing a week does nothing. Missing two months does nothing. The questions keep arriving, and the ones that went unanswered are still sitting there to come back to. If they know they need more time they can also put their account on hold for a few weeks or a few months.


Plenty of people answer in bursts. A quiet Sunday, four stories. Then nothing until the following month. The finished book does not record which weeks were skipped.


## Access doesn't stop when the plan year ends


This is the part that puts most people’s minds at rest. When the plan year is over, your storyteller can still write new stories for questions they've already received, edit existing ones, add photos and order copies of the book. The stories stay available to read and edit, and they remain private and owned by them.


If they want to keep receiving weekly questions and carry on, the plan can be renewed. If they would rather stop receiving questions and finish at their own pace, they can do that instead, and nothing is lost either way.


## The book gets printed whenever they are ready


Their book will never be automatically printed with gaps in it, and they'll always retain access to print new copies at any time.


They decide when it is done. That might be at eleven months, because they want it for a birthday. It might be at two years, because they got absorbed in one chapter and wanted to do it properly. Both produce a hardcover book and every Storyworth plan includes at least one hard cover book copy.


They can also download a free audiobook or e-book version at any time, which is a useful somebody wants to share stories with family before the printed copy exists.


## Short answers count


A lot of the worry about finishing is really a worry about story length.


Some memories need several pages. Some need three sentences, and three sentences about their grandmother’s kitchen is worth more than a page of padding. Your storyteller can write as much or as little as a question deserves, and adding a photos with captions often says the rest.


Telling them that explicitly, at the point you give the gift, removes most of the pressure they are about to put on themselves.


## If they stall, the format has a way back in


When somebody goes quiet, it is usually one of four things, and each has a fix.


**The question didn't land.** They can reword it, write their own, pick a different one from the question library, or let us create questions for them with Magic questions.


**Writing feels like work.** They can share stories by phone instead, on an ordinary call, and what they say is transcribed into their memoir. Switching between writing and talking needs no setup.


**They aren't sure what to say.** They can try a Magic Interview. We'll ask thoughtful follow up questions to bring out a story's details to life. Then we'll transform the conversation into a written story.


**They lost momentum.** Someone else in the family can join a Family Call and ask them
questions directly, which is often easier than facing a blank page alone.


## What to look for if you are comparing services


This question is worth asking of any memoir service you are considering, including Remento, Memorygram, StoryTerrace, Storii, My Life in a Book, Meminto, MyStories and Memowrite. The policies differ.


1. **What happens to the stories when the subscription ends?** Ask specifically whether they can still be read, edited and printed.
2. **Is there a deadline on printing the book?** Some services tie printing to an active subscription window.
3. **Can you export everything?** Ask what you can download, and in what format, if you ever want to leave.


Those three answers tell you what you are actually buying.
